articleTitle: REPRÉSENTATIONS GALOISIENNES ASSOCIÉES AUX COURBES HYPERELLIPTIQUES LISSES
abstract: In 2003, Kedlaya gave an algorithm to compute the zeta function associated to a hyperelliptic curve over a finite field, by computing the rigid cohomology of the curve. Edixhoven remarked that it is actually possible to compute the crystalline cohomology of the curve, which is a lattice in the rigid cohomology. Following a method of Wach, we explain how to use this lattice to compute the (φ, Γ)-module associated to an hyperelliptic curve. En 2003, Kedlaya a donné un algorithme pour calculer la fonction zêta d’une courbe hyperelliptique sur un corps fini, en calculant la cohomologie rigide de la courbe. Edixhoven a remarqué qu’on pouvait en fait calculer la cohomologie cristalline de la courbe, qui est un réseau dans la cohomologie rigide. Nous expliquons comment utiliser ce réseau pour calculer le (φ, Γ)-module associé à une courbe hyperelliptique, en suivant une méthode due à Wach.

articleTitle: CORRIGENDUM “REPRESENTATION TYPE OF FROBENIUS-LUSZTIG KERNELS”
THE UNIVERSAL η-INVARIANT FOR MANIFOLDS WITH BOUNDARY
abstract: We extend the theory of the universal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta$</tex>-invariant to the case of bordism groups of manifolds with boundaries. This allows the construction of secondary descendants of the universal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta$</tex>-invariant. We obtain an interpretation of Laures’ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>-invariant as an example of this general construction. As an aside, we improve a recent result by Han–Zhang about the modularity of a certain formal power series of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\eta$</tex>-invariants.

articleTitle: LOCALIZATION AND PROJECTIONS ON BI-PARAMETER BMO
abstract: We prove that for any operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> on bi–parameter BMO the identity factors through <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Id-T$</tex>. Bourgain's localization method provides the conceptual framework of our proof. It consists of replacing the factorization problem on the non-separable bi-parameter BMO by its localized, finite dimensional counterpart. We solve the resulting finite dimensional factorization problems by exploiting the geometry and combinatorics of colored dyadic rectangles.

articleTitle: COBORDISM OBSTRUCTIONS TO INDEPENDENT VECTOR FIELDS
abstract: We define an invariant for the existence of r pointwise linearly independent sections in the tangent bundle of a closed manifold. For low values of r, explicit computations of the homotopy groups of certain Thom spectra combined with classical obstruction theory identifies this invariant as the top obstruction to the existence of the desired sections. In particular, this shows that the top obstruction is an invariant of the underlying manifold in these cases, which is not true in general. The invariant is related to cobordism theory, and this gives rise to an identification of the invariant in terms of well-known invariants. As a corollary to the computations, we can also compute the low-dimensional homotopy groups of the embedded cobordism category introduced in Galatius et al. [The homotopy type of the cobordism category, Acta Math. 202 (2009), 195–239].

articleTitle: DUAL SPACES AND JOHN–NIRENBERG INEQUALITIES OF MARTINGALE HARDY–LORENTZ–KARAMATA SPACES
abstract: In this paper, the generalized BMO martingale spaces are introduced as the dual spaces of martingale Hardy–Lorentz–Karamata spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{p,q,b}^s$</tex>, which completes the very recent result [Quart. J. Math. 65 (2014), 985–1009] in the case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\lt p\leq 1, 1\lt q\lt \infty$</tex>. Moreover, by duality we obtain a new John–Nirenberg theorem when the stochastic basis is regular.

articleTitle: COMPACT HOMOGENEOUS SPACES WITH POSITIVE EULER CHARACTERISTIC AND THEIR ‘STRANGE FORMULAE’
abstract: In this note, we prove a generalization of the ‘strange formula’ of Freudenthal and de-Vries for compact homogeneous spaces with positive Euler characteristic. As a corollary, we obtain a new proof of the original formula. We also apply our results to computing a topological invariant used to study hyper-Kähler structures.

articleTitle: ON ULTRAFRIABLE INTEGERS
abstract: Say that an integer n is y-ultrafriable if its canonical decomposition is free of prime powers exceeding y. We investigate the asymptotic behaviour of the distribution function Ƴ(x, y), equal to the number of y-ultrafriable integers not exceeding x. The study being restricted to the range ψ(y)>2 log x (where ψ denotes Chebyshev's function) by a symmetry argument, and writing Ψ(x, y) for the number of y-friable integers not exceeding x, β=β(x, y) for the saddle point associated to the Dirichlet series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Z(s,y):=\prod_{p\leqslant y}(1-p^{-(\nu_{p}+1) s})/( 1-p^{-s})$</tex> where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\nu_{p}:=\lfloor(\log y)/\log p\rfloor$</tex>, we obtain full description via a number of effective estimates, qualitative versions of which may be stated as follows:<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Upsilon(x, y)\sim\Psi(x, y)\Leftrightarrow y/(\log x)^{2}\to \infty\ (x\to \infty)$</tex>;<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Upsilon(x, y) = o(\Psi(x, y))\Leftrightarrow y/(\log x)^{2}\to 0\ (x\to \infty)$</tex>;<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Upsilon(x, y)\sim x^{\beta} Z(\beta, y)G(\beta \sqrt{\sigma_{2}})\ (x\to \infty, 2 \log x < \psi(y)\leqslant (\log x)^{3})$</tex>.Here <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{2}:=\hbox{d}^{2}\{\log Z(\beta, y)\}/\hbox{d} s^{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G(z):=\hbox{e}^{z^{2}/2}\int_{z}^{\infty} \hbox{e}^{-t^{2}/2}\hbox{d}t/\sqrt{2\pi}$</tex> (z>0). Moreover, the phase transition between domains (i) and (ii) is quantitatively described in terms of the Dickman function, the Gaussian behaviour as log x approaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\frac{1}{2}\psi(y)$</tex> is made explicit, and a quantitative estimate for the local behaviour with respect to the variable x is derived.

articleTitle: CHARACTER SUMS WITH PIATETSKI-SHAPIRO SEQUENCES
abstract: For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c >1$</tex>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c \notin \mathbb Z$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\chi$</tex> a primitive character <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\hbox{mod }}q)$</tex>, we estimate the sum<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[\sum _{x \lt n \le x +y} \chi ([n^c]).\]$$</tex>Our results complement earlier work of Banks and Shparlinski. We also give a new bound for the least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[n^c]$</tex> is a quadratic non-residue <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({\rm mod}\ q)$</tex>, in the case of prime <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex>, for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \lt c \lt \tfrac {371}{309}$</tex>.

articleTitle: VALEURS FRIABLES D'UNE FORME QUADRATIQUE ET D'UNE FORME LINÉAIRE
abstract: Given ℛ a set of integers, F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) a linear form and F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) an irreducible quadratic form, we study in this work the cardinality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\#\{1\leqslant n_1,n_2\leqslant x:F_1(n_1,n_2)\in\mathcal{R}\hbox{ and }P^+(F_2(n_1,n_2))\leqslant y\},$$</tex> where P<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>(n) denotes the greatest prime factor of an integer n. In particular, we give an asymptotic formula for the number of pairs of integers (n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) in the square [1, x]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> such that F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) are both y-friable in the range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\exp\left(\frac{\log x(\log\log\log x)^{1+\varepsilon}}{\log\log x}\right)\leqslant y\leqslant x^{2}.$$</tex>

articleTitle: ON DEFINING AW*-ALGEBRAS AND RICKART C*-ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> be a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}^{* }$</tex>-algebra. It is shown that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm AW}^{* }$</tex>-algebra if, and only if, each maximal abelian self-adjoint (m.a.s.a.) subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is monotone complete. An analogous result is proved for Rickart <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}^{* }$</tex>-algebras; a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}^{* }$</tex>-algebra is a Rickart <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm C}^{* }$</tex>-algebra if, and only if, it is unital and each m.a.s.a. subalgebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> is monotone <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma$</tex>-complete.

articleTitle: THE SPECTRUM OF VOLTERRA OPERATORS ON WEIGHTED SPACES OF ENTIRE FUNCTIONS
abstract: We investigate the spectrum of the Volterra operator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_g$</tex> with symbol an entire function <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g$</tex>, when it acts on weighted Banach spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_v^{\infty }({\mathbb {C}})$</tex> of entire functions with sup-norms and when it acts on Hörmander algebras <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_p$</tex> or <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A^0_p$</tex>.

articleTitle: CONGRUENCES FOR PARTITION PAIRS WITH CONDITIONS
abstract: We prove congruences for the number of partition pairs <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\pi _1,\pi _2)$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi _1$</tex> is non-empty, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s(\pi _1)\le s(\pi _2)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell (\pi _2)\lt 2s(\pi _1)$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s(\pi )$</tex> is the smallest part and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell (\pi )$</tex> is the largest part of a partition. The proofs use Bailey's Lemma and a generalized Lambert series identity of Chan. We also discuss how a partition pair crank gives combinatorial refinements of these congruences.

articleTitle: ON C*-ALGEBRAS WHICH CANNOT BE DECOMPOSED INTO TENSOR PRODUCTS WITH BOTH FACTORS INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL
abstract: We prove that C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex>-algebras which, as Banach spaces, are Grothendieck cannot be decomposed into a tensor product of two infinite-dimensional C<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex>-algebras. By a result of Pfitzner, this class contains all von Neumann algebras and their norm-quotients. We thus complement a recent result of Ghasemi who established a similar conclusion for the class of SAW<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^{\ast }$</tex>-algebras.

articleTitle: SQUARE-FREE VALUES OF POLYNOMIALS EVALUATED AT PRIMES OVER A FUNCTION FIELD
abstract: We study a function field version of a classical problem concerning square-free values of polynomials evaluated at primes. We show that for a square-free polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f\in {\mathbb {F}_q}[t][x]$</tex>, there is a limiting density as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\to \infty$</tex> of primes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P \in {\mathbb {F}_q}[t]$</tex> of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f(P)$</tex> is square-free.Over the integers, the analogous result is only known when all irreducible factors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> have degree at most 3.

articleTitle: NORMALITY OF THE THUE–MORSE SEQUENCE ALONG PIATETSKI-SHAPIRO SEQUENCES
abstract: We prove that for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1<c<4/3$</tex> the subsequence of the Thue–Morse sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf t$</tex> indexed by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lfloor n^c\rfloor $</tex> defines a normal sequence, that is, each finite sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon _0,\ldots ,\varepsilon _{T-1})\in \{0,1\}^T$</tex> occurs as a contiguous subsequence of the sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n\mapsto \mathbf t(\lfloor n^c\rfloor )$</tex> with asymptotic frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{-T}$</tex>.

articleTitle: MINKOWSKI DECOMPOSITION AND GENERATORS OF THE MOVING CONE FOR TORIC VARIETIES
abstract: We prove that for smooth projective toric varieties, the Okounkov body of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>-invariant pseudo-effective divisor with respect to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>-invariant flag decomposes as a finite Minkowski sum of indecomposable polytopes, and that the set of these polytopes corresponds to a finite Minkowski basis whose elements span the extremal rays in the secondary fan. In fact, the Minkowski basis does not depend on the choice of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T$</tex>-invariant flag. Moreover, we present an algorithm that computes the Minkowski basis.

articleTitle: ON INTERPOLATION OF THE MEASURE OF NON-COMPACTNESS BY THE COMPLEX METHOD
abstract: The measure of non-compactness of operators between complex interpolation spaces is studied. An estimate of this measure, under the Calderón approximation condition, is proved. Examples of Banach couples satisfying the mentioned condition are provided. An estimate of the essential spectral radius of an operator under complex interpolation is also given.

articleTitle: POLYNOMIAL VALUES IN SUBFIELDS AND AFFINE SUBSPACES OF FINITE FIELDS
abstract: For an integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex>, a prime power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q$</tex> and a polynomial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> over a finite field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb F}}_{q^r}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$q^r$</tex> elements, we obtain an upper bound on the frequency of elements in an orbit generated by iterations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> which fall in a proper subfield of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb F}}_{q^r}$</tex>. We also obtain similar results for elements in affine subspaces of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb F}}_{q^r}$</tex>, considered as a linear space over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{\mathbb F}}_q$</tex>.

articleTitle: ON THE NON-VANISHING OF DIRICHLET L-FUNCTIONS AT THE CENTRAL POINT
abstract: We investigate the consequences of natural conjectures of Montgomery type on the non-vanishing of Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions at the central point. We first justify these conjectures using probabilistic arguments. We then show using a result of Bombieri, Friedlander and Iwaniec, and a result of the author that they imply that almost all Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions do not vanish at the central point. We also deduce a quantitative upper bound for the proportion of Dirichlet <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex>-functions for which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L(\frac {1}{2},\chi )=0$</tex>.

articleTitle: INCOMPLETE EXPONENTIAL SUMS OVER EXPONENTIAL FUNCTIONS
abstract: We extend some methods of bounding exponential sums of the type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum_{n\le N}\,{\rm e}^{2\pi {\rm i}ag^{n}/p}$</tex> to deal with the case when g is not necessarily a primitive root. We also show that some recent results of Shkredov concerning additive properties of multiplicative subgroups imply new bounds for the sums under consideration.

articleTitle: η-INVARIANT AND MODULAR FORMS
abstract: We show that the Atiyah–Patodi–Singer reduced η-invariant of the twisted Dirac operator on a closed 4m−1-dimensional spin manifold, with the twisted bundle being the Witten bundle appearing in the theory of elliptic genus, is a meromorphic modular form of weight 2m up to an integral q-series. We prove this result by combining our construction of certain modular characteristic forms associated to a generalized Witten bundle on spin<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup>-manifolds with a deep topological theorem due to Hopkins.

articleTitle: ON A STABILITY PROPERTY OF SKYRME-RELATED ENERGY FUNCTIONALS
abstract: We study the stability of critical maps from (or into) spheres with respect to the symplectic Dirichlet and σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> energies which are the fourth power terms in Skyrme-type sigma-models.

articleTitle: PRACTICAL NUMBERS AND THE DISTRIBUTION OF DIVISORS
abstract: An integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> is called practical if every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m\le n$</tex> can be written as a sum of distinct divisors of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>. We show that the number of practical numbers below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> is asymptotic to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$c x/\log x$</tex>, as conjectured by Margenstern. We also give an asymptotic estimate for the number of integers below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> whose maximum ratio of consecutive divisors is at most <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex>, valid uniformly for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t\ge 2$</tex>.

articleTitle: LARGE SIEVE INEQUALITIES WITH GENERAL POLYNOMIAL MODULI
abstract: We prove a large sieve inequality with moduli of general polynomial form. The version with moduli being the product of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex> many <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex>th powers has an application to counting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell$</tex>-tuples of consecutive integers with high index of composition, a problem related to the abc-conjecture.

articleTitle: NOTE SUR LES VALEURS MOYENNES CRIBLÉES DE CERTAINES FONCTIONS ARITHMÉTIQUES
abstract: We provide, in a wide range of the parameters, an estimate for the mean-value over sifted integers of certain arithmetic functions with Dirichlet series analytically close to 1/ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(s), where K is a number field and ζ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> its Dedekind zeta function.

articleTitle: DISTINCT ZEROS OF THE RIEMANN ZETA-FUNCTION
abstract: In this paper, we prove that more than 66.036% of zeros of the Riemann zeta-function are distinct.

articleTitle: CLONING AND BROADCASTING IN OPERATOR ALGEBRAS
abstract: We investigate cloning and broadcasting in the general operator algebra framework in arbitrary dimension, generalizing thus results obtained so far in finite dimension, and for the full algebra of operators on a Hilbert space. Moreover, we also weaken the assumption of complete positivity of the broadcasting (cloning) operation. It turns out that some results can be expressed in terms of modular theory for W*-algebras, in particular, the Connes cocycles are used for a characterization of broadcastability.

articleTitle: ON THE BRAUER INDECOMPOSABILITY OF SCOTT MODULES
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>, and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> be a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-subgroup of a finite group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>. We give sufficient conditions for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kG$</tex>-Scott module <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Sc}(G,P)$</tex> with vertex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> to remain indecomposable under the Brauer construction with respect to any subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex>. This generalizes similar results for the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P$</tex> is abelian. The background motivation for this note is the fact that the Brauer indecomposability of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex>-permutation bimodule is a key step towards showing that the module under consideration induces a stable equivalence of Morita type, which then may possibly be lifted to a derived equivalence.

articleTitle: 112 LINES ON SMOOTH QUARTIC SURFACES (CHARACTERISTIC 3)
abstract: Over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>, we prove that there are no smooth quartic surfaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S \subset {\mathbb {P}}^3_k$</tex> with more than 112 lines. Moreover, the surface with 112 lines is projectively equivalent over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar k$</tex> to the Fermat quartic. As a key ingredient, we derive a characteristic-free upper bound for the number of lines met by a conic on a smooth quartic surface.

articleTitle: A GENERALIZATION OF A GRAPH THEORY MERTENS’ THEOREM: ABELIAN COVERING CASE
abstract: In 1874, Franz Mertens proved the so-called Mertens’ third theorem in number theory, and after just 100 years, Kenneth S. Williams generalized it. In the previous papers, the first and the second authors presented a graph-theoretic analogue to the Mertens’ third theorem. In this paper, we generalize it along the lines of Williams.

articleTitle: DIFFEOMORPHIC APPROXIMATION OF CONTINUOUS ALMOST EVERYWHERE INJECTIVE SOBOLEV DEFORMATIONS IN THE PLANE
abstract: In this note, we prove that given a continuous Sobolev <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W^{1,p}$</tex> deformation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 < p < \infty $</tex>, from a planar domain to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {R}^2$</tex> which is injective almost everywhere, we can find a sequence <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_k$</tex> of diffeomorphisms with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_k - f \in W^{1,p}_0$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_k \to f$</tex> uniformly and in the Sobolev norm.

articleTitle: BAIRE CLASSES OF NON-SEPARABLE L1-PREDUALS
abstract: Let X be an L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-predual, non-separable in general. We show that the intrinsic Baire classes of X can be identified with the spaces of odd Baire functions on the set ext B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X*</inf> of the extreme points of the dual unit ball B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X*</inf> in the case when ext B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X*</inf> satisfies some topological assumptions. This generalizes results of Lindenstrauss and Wulbert from [On the classification of the Banach spaces whose duals are L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> spaces, J. Funct. Anal. 4 (1969), 332–349], Jellett in [On affine extensions of continuous functions defined on the extreme boundary of a Choquet simplex, Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (1) 36 (1985), 71–73] and of ours in [Baire Classes of L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>-preduals and C*-algebras, 2013.: http://www.karlin.mff.cuni.cz/spurny/articles.php].

articleTitle: HIGHER DIFFERENTIABILITY FOR SOLUTIONS OF A CLASS OF PARABOLIC SYSTEMS WITH L1, θ- DATA
abstract: We study the higher differentiability of the very weak solution of the Cauchy–Dirichlet problem associated to the linear parabolic system with Hölder continuous coefficients and L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> right-hand side of the form<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{align*} \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial t} -{\rm div}(A(x,t)Du) &= \mu \quad \mbox{in } \Omega \,{\times}\,]0, T[,\\ u &= 0 \quad \mbox{on } \partial \Omega \,{\times}\,]0, T[,\\ u &= 0 \quad \mbox{on } \Omega \times \{ 0\}. \end{align*}$$</tex>

articleTitle: ACTIONS OF THE N-STRAND BRAID GROUPS ON THE FREE GROUP OF RANK N WHICH ARE SIMILAR TO THE ARTIN REPRESENTATION
abstract: We classify an action of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>-strand braid group on the free group of rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, which is similar to the Artin representation in the sense that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>th generator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma _{i}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B_{n}$</tex> acts so that it fixes all free generators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x_{j}$</tex> except <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$j = i,i+1$</tex>. We determine all such representations and discuss knot invariants coming from such representations.

articleTitle: CURVATURE OF FIELDS OF QUANTUM HILBERT SPACES
abstract: We show that using the family of adapted Kähler polarizations of the phase space of a compact, simply connected, Riemannian symmetric space of rank 1, the field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H^{\rm corr}$</tex> of quantum Hilbert spaces produced by geometric quantization, including the half-form correction, is flat if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is the three-dimensional sphere and not even projectively flat otherwise.

articleTitle: WEYL'S INEQUALITY AND SYSTEMS OF FORMS
abstract: Let F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> be integer forms of degree d ≥ 2 in s variables. Relaxing the non-singularity condition in a well-known result by Birch, we establish the expected Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic formula for the density of integer points on the intersection F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = ··· = F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 0, providing that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\begin{equation} s \gt \max_{\textbf{a} \in \mathbb{Z}^r \backslash \{\boldsymbol{0}\}} \dim V_{\textbf{a}}^* + r(r+1) (d-1) 2^{d-1},\end{equation}$$</tex> where V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> = {x ∈ ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>: ∇(a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(x) + ··· + a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>(x)) = 0}. In the same context, we also improve on previous work by Schmidt and show that the expected Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic formula holds true, providing that each form in the rational pencil of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> has rank exceeding 2r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 2r (d = 2); h-invariant exceeding 8r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 8r (d = 3); h-invariant exceeding φ(d) (d − 1) 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d−1</sup> r(r + 1) for a certain function φ(d) when d≥4. In particular, if F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> are rational quadratic forms, each form in their complex pencil has rank exceeding 2r<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 2r, and the intersection F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> = ··· = F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 0 has a non-singular real zero, then this intersection also has a non-trivial rational zero. For r = 1, this recovers a classical result by Meyer.Our new tool, which is of interest in itself, is a variant of Weyl's inequality for general systems of forms that is useful in situations such as those above where one knows a certain lower rank (or dimension of singular locus) bound for all forms in the rational pencil of the given ones.

articleTitle: THE GORENSTEIN DEFECT CATEGORY
abstract: We consider the homotopy category of complexes of projective modules over a Noetherian ring. Truncation at degree zero induces a fully faithful triangle functor from the totally acyclic complexes to the singularity category. We show that if the ring is either Artin or commutative Noetherian local, then the functor is dense if and only if the ring is Gorenstein. Motivated by this, we define the Gorenstein defect category of the ring, a category which in some sense measures how far the ring is from being Gorenstein.

articleTitle: DIOPHANTINE APPROXIMATION ON LINES WITH PRIME CONSTRAINTS
abstract: We study the problem of Diophantine approximation on lines in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with prime numerator and denominator.

articleTitle: RIGIDITY OF QUASI-ISOMETRIES OF HMN ASSOCIATED WITH NON-DIAGONALIZABLE DERIVATION OF THE HEISENBERG ALGEBRA
abstract: We study quasi-isometries of the homogeneous manifold with negative curvature associated with a non-diagonalizable derivation of the Heisenberg algebra. We show that all quasi-isometries are almost isometries. We prove this by finding all the quasi-symmetric maps on the ideal boundary.

articleTitle: QUANTUM CHROMATIC NUMBERS VIA OPERATOR SYSTEMS
abstract: We define several new types of quantum chromatic numbers of a graph and characterize them in terms of operator system tensor products. We establish inequalities between these chromatic numbers and other parameters of graphs studied in the literature and exhibit a link between them and non-signalling correlation boxes.

articleTitle: ON THE GROUP STRUCTURE OF ${[\Omega \mathbb{S}^2,\Omega Y}$
abstract: Let J(X) denote the James construction on a space X and J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(X) be the nth stage of the James filtration of J(X). It is known that [J(X), Ω Y] ≅ lim <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">←</inf> [J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(X), Ω Y] for any space Y. When <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, the circle, J(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>)=Ω Σ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>=Ω <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Furthermore, there is a bijection between [J(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>), Ω Y] and the product <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\prod_{i=2}^{\infty} \pi_{i}(Y)$</tex>, as sets. In this paper, we describe the group structure of [J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>), Ω Y] by determining the co-multiplication structure on the suspension Σ J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{S}^2$</tex><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>).

articleTitle: PARABOLIC EQUATIONS WITH p,q-GROWTH: THE SUBQUADRATIC CASE
abstract: We are interested in existence and regularity results for weak solutions of parabolic equations of the type<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[\partial _t u- \operatorname {div}\,a(x,t,Du)=0\]$$</tex>on a parabolic space time cylinder <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega _T$</tex>. The vector field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> is assumed to satisfy a non-standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p,q$</tex>-growth condition. We treat the subquadratic case, where<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[\frac {2n}{n+2}\lt p\lt 2 \quad {\text {and}} \quad p\leq q \lt p+ \frac {4}{n+2}\]$$</tex>holds. We show existence of weak s<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u \in L^p(0,T;W^{1,p}(\Omega )) \cap L^q_{\mathrm {loc}}(0,T;W^{1,q}_{\mathrm {loc}}(\Omega ))$</tex> for the Cauchy–Dirichlet problem associated to the parabolic equation from above. Further, a local bound for the spatial gradient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Du$</tex> is established. The results cover for example equations of the type<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[\partial _t u = \operatorname {div} (\alpha (x,t) (\mu ^2+ |Du|^2)^{(p-2)/2}Du) + \operatorname {div}(\beta (x,t)(\mu ^2 + |Du|^2)^{(q-2)/2}Du)\]$$</tex>with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \in [0,1]$</tex> and suitable functions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha (x,t)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta (x,t)$</tex>. We emphasize that the results cover the singular case <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu =0$</tex>.

articleTitle: FONCTIONS À VARIATION BORNÉE ET CLASSE DE GODBILLON–VEY
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S: (V_{1}, F_{1}) \rightarrow (V_{2}, F_{2})$</tex> be a foliated continuous map between smooth manifolds with codimension 1 smooth foliations, transversely oriented. If the transverse component of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> has bounded variation with derivative in the Lebesgue class of measure, then the image by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^* : H^3(V_{2},F_{2}) \rightarrow H^3(V_{1},F_{1})$</tex> of the Godbillon–Vey class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{2}$</tex> is the Godbillon–Vey class of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{1}$</tex>. This solves partially a question raised by Etienne Ghys.

articleTitle: CONVERGENCE OF AN APPROXIMATION FOR ROTATIONALLY SYMMETRIC TWO-PHASE LIPID BILAYER MEMBRANES
abstract: We consider a diffuse interface approximation for the lipid phases of rotationally symmetric two-phase bilayer membranes and rigorously derive its Γ-limit. In particular, we prove that limit vesicles are C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> across interfaces, which justifies a regularity assumption that is widely made in formal asymptotic and numerical studies. Moreover, a limit membrane may consist of several topological spheres, which are connected at the axis of revolution and resemble complete buds of the vesicle.

articleTitle: SOME ASSOCIATIVE SUBMANIFOLDS OF THE SQUASHED 7-SPHERE
abstract: The squashed 7-sphere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{7}$</tex> is a 7-sphere with an Einstein metric given by the canonical variation and its cone <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {R}^{8} - \{0 \}$</tex> has full holonomy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Spin}(7)$</tex>. There is a canonical calibrating 4-form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex> on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb {R}^{8} - \{0 \}$</tex>. A minimal 3-submanifold in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{7}$</tex> is called associative if its cone is calibrated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Phi$</tex>.In this paper, we classify two types of fundamental associative submanifolds in the squashed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S^{7}$</tex>. One is obtained by the intersection with a 4-plane and the other is homogeneous. Then we study their infinitesimal associative deformations and explicitly show that all of them are integrable.

articleTitle: POSTORDER REARRANGEMENT OPERATORS
abstract: We investigate the rearrangement of the Haar system induced by the postorder on the set of dyadic intervals in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[0,1]$</tex> with length greater than or equal to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2^{-N}$</tex>. By means of operator norms on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hbox {BMO}_N$</tex> we prove that the postorder has maximal distance to the usual lexicographic order.

articleTitle: BIFURCATION OF PLANE-TO-PLANE MAP-GERMS OF CORANK 2
abstract: We describe the bifurcation diagrams of plane-to-plane map-germs of corank 2 up to<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>-codimension 4, and draw some new pictures. Two applications are presented: First, we study the affine differential geometry of crosscaps in 3-space by means of analyzing singularities of projections of the singular surface to the plane. Secondly, we give some new examples of generic two-dimensional bifurcations of D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-type planar caustics.

articleTitle: A TORELLI-TYPE PROBLEM FOR LOGARITHMIC BUNDLES OVER PROJECTIVE VARIETIES
abstract: We investigate the logarithmic bundles associated to arrangements of hypersurfaces with a fixed degree in a smooth projective variety. We then specialize to the case when the variety is a quadric hypersurface and a multiprojective space to prove a Torelli-type theorem in some cases.

articleTitle: DERANGEMENTS IN PRIMITIVE PERMUTATION GROUPS, WITH AN APPLICATION TO CHARACTER THEORY
abstract: Let G be a finite primitive permutation group and let κ(G) be the number of conjugacy classes of derangements in G. By a classical theorem of Jordan, κ(G) ⩾ 1. In this paper, we classify the groups G with κ(G)=1, and we use this to obtain new results on the structure of finite groups with an irreducible complex character that vanishes on a unique conjugacy class. We also obtain detailed structural information on the groups with κ(G)=2, including a complete classification for almost simple groups.

articleTitle: APPROXIMATION AND CONVEX DECOMPOSITION BY EXTREMALS AND THE λ-FUNCTION IN JBW*-TRIPLES
abstract: We establish new estimates to compute the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-function of Aron and Lohman on the unit ball of a JB<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^* $</tex>-triple. It is established that for every Brown–Pedersen quasi-invertible element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> in a JB<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^* $</tex>-triple <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> we have<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[{\rm dist} (a, \mathfrak {E} (E_1)) = \max \{ 1- m_q (a), \|a\|-1\} ,\]$$</tex>where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathfrak {E} (E_1)$</tex> denotes the set of extreme points of the closed unit ball <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_1$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex>. It is proved that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (a) = ({1+m_q (a)})/{2},$</tex> for every Brown–Pedersen quasi-invertible element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_1$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m_q (a)$</tex> is the square root of the quadratic conorm of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>. For an element <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_1$</tex> which is not Brown–Pedersen quasi-invertible, we can only estimate that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda (a)\leq \frac 12 (1-\alpha _q (a))$</tex>. A complete description of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-function on the closed unit ball of every JBW<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^* $</tex>-triple is also provided, and as a consequence, we prove that every JBW<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$^* $</tex>-triple satisfies the uniform <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>-property.

articleTitle: AMENABILITY AND MODULES FOR ARENS PRODUCT ALGEBRAS
abstract: Given a Banach algebra A, we introduce the notion of a left dual Banach algebra (LDBA) over A, and we establish that every LDBA over A is a left Arens product algebra over A. This can be viewed as a Banach algebraic version of the fact that every semigroup compactification is a Gelfand compactification. We show how A-module operations can be extended to obtain module operations for left Arens product algebras over A that satisfy attractive w*-continuity properties. We introduce a notion of left Connes amenability for LDBAs, and show that the amenability of a locally compact group G is equivalent to left Connes amenability of either the bidual L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">**</sup> of its group algebra L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G), or the dual LUC(G)* where LUC(G) is the space of left uniformly continuous functions on G.

articleTitle: A TWISTED HOMOLOGY FIBRATION CRITERION AND THE TWISTED GROUP-COMPLETION THEOREM
abstract: The purpose of this note is to clarify some details in McDuff and Segal's proof of the group-completion theorem in McDuff and Segal [Homology fibrations and the ‘group-completion’ theorem, Invent. Math. 31 (1975/76), 279–284] and generalize this and the homology fibration criterion of McDuff [Configuration spaces of positive and negative particles, Topology 14 (1975), 91–107] to homology with twisted coefficients. This will be used in Miller and Palmer [Scanning for oriented configuration spaces, preprint, 2014] to identify the limiting homology of ‘oriented’ configuration spaces, which doubly cover the classical configuration spaces of distinct unordered points in a manifold.

articleTitle: ON AUTOMORPHISMS OF FREE CENTER-BY-METABELIAN LIE ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{n}$</tex> be the free center-by-metabelian Lie algebra of finite rank <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex>, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geq 2$</tex>, over a field <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> of characteristic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0$</tex>. We study the automorphism group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{n})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{n}$</tex> by means of a topology. Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{C_{n}}$</tex> be the group of tame automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{n}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_{n}(K)$</tex> be the general linear group. It is shown that for any finite subset <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> of IA-automorphisms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{2}$</tex>, the subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{2})$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm GL}_{2}(K)$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> is not dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{2})$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n = 3$</tex>, the subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{3})$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{C_{3}}$</tex> and two more IA-automorphisms is dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{3})$</tex>. For <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geq 4$</tex>, the subgroup of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{n})$</tex> generated by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{C_{n}}$</tex> and one more IA-automorphism is dense in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm Aut}(C_{n})$</tex>.

articleTitle: ON HIGGS BUNDLES ON ELLIPTIC SURFACES
abstract: Let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi : X \rightarrow C$</tex> be a relatively minimal non-isotrivial elliptic surface over the field of complex numbers, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g(C) \geq 2$</tex>. In this article, we demonstrate an equivalence between the category of semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>, and the category of semistable Higgs bundles on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> with vanishing second Chern class, and determinant a vertical divisor.

articleTitle: COCYCLES OF ISOMETRIES AND DENSENESS OF DOMINATION
abstract: We consider the problem of approximating a linear cocycle (or, more generally, a vector bundle automorphism) over a fixed base dynamics by another cocycle admitting a dominated splitting. We prove that the possibility of doing so depends only on the homotopy class of the cocycle, provided that the base dynamics is a minimal diffeomorphism and the fiber dimension is at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3$</tex>. This result is obtained by means of a general theorem on the existence of almost invariant sections for fiberwise isometries of bundles with compact fibers and finite fundamental group. As another consequence of that theorem, we characterize almost coboundaries on compact Lie groups with finite center. The main novelty of the proofs is the use of a quantitative homotopy result due to Calder, Siegel and Williams.

articleTitle: REPRESENTATION OF SMALL INTEGERS BY BINARY FORMS
abstract: We establish some upper bounds for the number of integer solutions to the Thue inequality <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|F(x , y)| \leq m$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$F$</tex> is a binary form of degree <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n \geq 3$</tex> and with non-zero discriminant <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> is an integer. Our upper bounds are independent of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> is smaller than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|D|^{{1}/{4(n-1)}}$</tex>. We also consider the Thue equation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|F(x , y)| = m$</tex> and give some upper bounds for the number of its integral solutions. In the case of equation, our upper bounds will be independent of integer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex>, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m < |D|^{{1}/{2(n-1)}}$</tex>.

articleTitle: STRICTLY CONTINUOUS EXTENSION OF FUNCTIONALS WITH LINEAR GROWTH TO THE SPACE BV
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the integral functional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {F}[u]\colon {\mathrm {BV}}(\Omega ;{\mathbb {R}}^m)\to {\mathbb {R}}$</tex> defined by<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[\mathcal {F}[u]:=\int _\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,{\mathrm {d}}x+ \int _\Omega \int _0^1 f^\infty \left ( x,u^\theta (x),\frac {{\mathrm {d}}D^s u}{{\mathrm {d}}|D^s u|}(x)\right ) {\mathrm {d}}\theta \,{\mathrm {d}}|D^su|(x)\]$$</tex>is continuous over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm {BV}}(\Omega ;{\mathbb {R}}^m)$</tex>, with respect to the topology of area-strict convergence, a topology in which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({{W}}^{1,1}\cap {{C}}^\infty )(\Omega ;{\mathbb {R}}^m)$</tex> is dense. This provides conclusive justification for the treatment of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal {F}$</tex> as the natural extension of the functional<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$$\[u\mapsto \int _\Omega f(x,u(x),\nabla u(x))\,{\mathrm {d}}x,\]</tex>defined for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\in {{W}}^{1,1}(\Omega ;{\mathbb {R}}^m)$</tex>. This result is valid for a large class of integrands satisfying <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|f(x,y,A)|\leq C(1+ |y|^{d/(d-1)}+ |A|)$</tex> and its proof makes use of Reshetnyak's Continuity Theorem combined with a lifting map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu [u]\colon {\mathrm {BV}}(\Omega ;{\mathbb {R}}^m)\to {\mathbf {M}}(\Omega \times {\mathbb {R}}^m;{\mathbb {R}}^{m\times d})$</tex>. To obtain the theorem in the case where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> exhibits <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d/(d-1)$</tex> growth in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y$</tex> variable, an embedding result from the theory of concentration-compactness is also employed.

articleTitle: HOMOLOGICAL FINITENESS PROPERTIES OF WREATH PRODUCTS
abstract: We study the homological finiteness properties <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm FP}_m$</tex> of wreath products <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma = H \wr _X G$</tex>. We show that, when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> has infinite abelianization, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> is of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm FP}_m$</tex> if and only if both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> have type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm FP}_m$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> acts (diagonally) on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X^i$</tex> with stabilizers of type <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm FP}_{m-i}$</tex> and with finitely many orbits for all <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \leq i \leq m$</tex>.If furthermore <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex> is torsion-free, we give a criterion for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma$</tex> to be Bredon-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\rm FP}_m$</tex> with respect to the class of finite subgroups of <tex
